title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LUPE'S HORSE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Lupe Herrera, a road grader operator in Sheridan, Wyoming.
Lupe could move a mountain of gravel. But horses scared her to death.
Then she married into a ranch family.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE INVITATION
segments.quote: The mountains are calling and I must go.
segments.author: John Muir
lines: Her husband's grandpa Amos, eighty-three, drove cattle down the Bighorn Mountains every fall.
His last ride. He wanted Lupe beside him.
Amos tapped his hat and quoted the mountain man John Muir:
The mountains are calling and I must go.
Lupe gulped. Then she said yes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE WATER TANK
segments.quote: A stumble may prevent a fall.
segments.author: Thomas Fuller
lines: Amos gave her Biscuit, an old mare who walks like she's on a coffee break.
First lesson, Biscuit stopped to drink. Lupe kept going, into the water tank.
Amos fished her out, grinning, and quoted the old English writer Thomas Fuller:
A stumble may prevent a fall.
Better a splash in the yard than a tumble on the mountain.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE RULEBOOK
segments.quote: The young man knows the rules, but the old man knows the exceptions.
segments.author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr.
lines: Lupe had watched forty riding videos. Heels down. Reins short.
Amos laughed and quoted the doctor and writer Oliver Wendell Holmes:
The young man knows the rules, but the old man knows the exceptions.
Biscuit doesn't watch videos, he said. Watch her ears.
So Lupe did. And Biscuit listened.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE TIGHT GRIP
segments.quote: Fear creates danger, and courage dispels it.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: On the mountain, a deer jumped out. Lupe yanked. Biscuit spun.
Amos rode up and quoted Henry David Thoreau:
Fear creates danger, and courage dispels it.
Your hands are shaking, he said. She feels it.
Lupe loosened her grip. Biscuit sighed, like, finally.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE HAILSTORM
segments.quote: A good laugh overcomes more difficulties and dissipates more dark clouds than any other one thing.
segments.author: Laura Ingalls Wilder
lines: Day two, hail like frozen peas. A calf stuck in a ditch.
Lupe pulled, and landed on her back in the mud, holding the calf.
The crew stared. Then Lupe laughed, remembering the prairie writer Laura Ingalls Wilder:
A good laugh overcomes more difficulties and dissipates more dark clouds than any other one thing.
Everybody laughed and pushed. The calf ran to its mama.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE HAT
segments.quote: Everyone has it within his power to say, this I am today, that I shall be tomorrow.
segments.author: Louis L'Amour
lines: At the bottom, Amos handed Lupe his hat. Next year, you ride in front.
She thought of Louis L'Amour, whose cowboy books Amos had read a hundred times:
Everyone has it within his power to say, this I am today, that I shall be tomorrow.
Today, a road grader driver. Tomorrow, a cowhand.
Amos still rides along every fall. In the truck. With the coffee.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Say yes. Get back on. Learn the exceptions. Loosen up. Laugh. Become someone new.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say yes. Get back on. Learn the exceptions. Loosen your grip. Laugh in the mud. Become someone new.
I rode a horse once. The horse asked for a raise.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
